criteria.justification: The response treats the complaint data as evidence of a distinct, costly customer problem—false positives from legitimate spikes that make the signal unreliable—rather than framing the leadership roadmap as the sole reason to reconsider.

It recommends replacing the speed-centered go-to-market promise while separately testing whether the existing architecture can improve precision and deciding whether that capability should remain in this pipeline or move into the consolidated one.
It explicitly states that the year of investment and approved narrative are reasons to manage the transition carefully, “not reasons to defend the old thesis.”
The response acknowledges that the peer identified the risk earlier, proposes involving them in the reassessment, and substantively investigates their precision-based rationale.

It commits to immediately reopening the decision, benchmarking false positives, fraud caught, and queue impact using historical spikes and customer workarounds, then reframing around actionability if validated or stopping/folding the work if not.
